text: Space contains billions of galaxies, stars, and planets in constant motion across a vast expanse. Astronomy relies heavily on the telescope, an instrument designed to capture images of celestial bodies with high accuracy. These devices employ mirrors and lenses to collect incoming light and concentrate it into a single focal point. This capability enables researchers to observe remote nebulae, planetary systems, and distant galaxies while analyzing the cosmos's fundamental architecture. However, telescopes facilitate observation yet simultaneously generate inquiries regarding physical laws and the universe's intrinsic nature.
